briefings.title: 2026 Spring Innovation Keynote: Next Chapter of Autonomous Marketing
briefings.tldr: ActiveCampaign is shifting from marketing automation to "Autonomous Marketing," introducing Active Intelligence as a proactive strategic advisor that uses persistent memory and background "autonomous interactions" to deliver personalized marketing outcomes with minimal manual intervention.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
ActiveCampaign is shifting from marketing automation to "Autonomous Marketing," introducing Active Intelligence as a proactive strategic advisor that uses persistent memory and background "autonomous interactions" to deliver personalized marketing outcomes with minimal manual intervention.

## The Evolution to Autonomous Marketing
*   **Strategic Shift:** The platform has moved beyond simple automation recipes to a rebuilt core foundation centered on **Active Intelligence**, designed to act as an extension of the marketing team rather than just a tool.
*   **Core Pillars:** The new chapter of autonomous marketing focuses on three areas: deeper intelligence, smarter decisions, and faster results.
*   **Efficiency Gains:**
    *   **Time to Value:** Users can move from signup to their first campaign in minutes—8x faster than starting from scratch.
    *   **Workflow Speed:** Campaigns can be launched 3x faster using AI-generated flows and copy.
    *   **Resource Management:** Notable customer successes include a 95% reduction in time spent on email marketing (Frank and Sherri) and 10 hours saved per month on reporting (Parrish Law).

## New Capabilities: Memory and Personalization
*   **Memory AI:** The system learns from user behavior rather than just prompts. It observes manual edits—such as softening call-to-actions or narrowing SMS segments—to align future suggestions with the user’s specific "strategic instincts."
*   **Custom Instructions:** Users can now define four specific guardrails to ensure AI outputs remain on-brand:
    *   **Working Preferences:** How the AI should collaborate (e.g., "always ask clarifying questions").
    *   **Target Audience:** Detailed profiles of who the business serves (e.g., "small businesses seeking creative partnership").
    *   **Content Guidelines:** Specific tone and formatting rules (e.g., "use invitation language," "keep emails under 200 words").
    *   **Business Uniqueness:** Defining the competitive advantage and current top priorities.
*   **Autonomous Interactions:** Unlike traditional AI that requires a prompt to start, these features work in the background to surface "outcomes" (e.g., an optimized A/B test or a discovered high-value segment) rather than just tasks or alerts.

## Real-World Customer Impact & Insights
*   **Performance Metrics:**
    *   **Toss and Spin:** Achieved a 71% open rate on targeted emails (vs. 46% for blasts) and a 10x year-over-year revenue increase in February by using AI to drive relevance.
    *   **Analytics Mates:** Improved newsletter open rates from 33% to 45% through AI-driven time-of-day and subject line optimization.
    *   **University of Albany:** Increased enrollment by 27% operating as a one-person marketing team.
*   **Strategic "Why":** Gary Spagnoli (Analytics Mates) noted that the primary value of Active Intelligence is its ability to explain *why* certain campaigns perform better, providing insights that inform strategy outside of just email marketing.
*   **Deployment Advice:** Chris Clark (Toss and Spin) recommends segmenting data on the front end and treating Active Intelligence like a consultant by asking, "What can I do to grow my business?"

## Proactive Troubleshooting and Revenue Discovery
*   **Segment Discovery:** In a demonstration for a creative agency, the AI identified 284 "Creative Advocates"—past clients worth an average of $94,000 in lifetime value—who were being neglected with standard promotional content. 
    *   The AI suggested a "craft-led" nurture track that focused on the creative process rather than transactional referrals.
*   **Automated Diagnostics:** The system can identify "invisible" errors that dashboards miss. 
    *   **Example:** Identifying an automation timing error where "milestone" emails were being sent weeks early because the wait step was resolving against enrollment dates rather than milestone dates.
*   **Outcome-Based Workflow:** Instead of hours of diagnostic work, the AI presented a "Clean Fix" that allowed the user to re-enroll affected contacts and fix the logic in under two minutes.

> "The more we do, the smarter it gets, the more data it can analyze and the faster we can go... they can go fast without guessing."
> — **Chris Clark**, Founder and CEO, Toss and Spin

> "These are autonomous interactions, AI working in the background and surfacing outcomes when they're ready for you. Not alerts, not tasks, outcomes."
> — **Mamie**, Product Team, ActiveCampaign

> "The value really came from the why. It started to understand what messaging, which audiences do well. And that actually informed a lot of marketing strategies that even live outside of email marketing."
> — **Gary Spagnoli**, Founder and CEO, Analytics Mates

briefings.title: $250M Founder Joins Naval Ravikant to Disrupt Venture Capital | ft Ankur Nagpal
briefings.tldr: After exits with Teachable and Carry, Ankur Nagpal has joined AngelList to lead USVC—a pioneering public venture fund that utilizes recent SEC approvals to allow non-accredited investors to access private startup markets with as little as $500.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
After exits with Teachable and Carry, Ankur Nagpal has joined AngelList to lead USVC—a pioneering public venture fund that utilizes recent SEC approvals to allow non-accredited investors to access private startup markets with as little as $500.

## The Shift from Founder to "Employee"
*   **The Carry Acquisition:** Nagpal recently sold his second company, Carry, to AngelList. While the business was successful ($4M ARR in three years), he recognized it was a "solid business" rather than a massive venture outlier.
*   **Working with Naval Ravikant:** Nagpal accepted a GP role at AngelList to run USVC, a project Naval Ravikant has envisioned for a decade. This marks Nagpal's first time being an employee since an internship at age 18.
*   **Radical Honesty:** Nagpal rejects the "false bravado" common in Silicon Valley. He attributes his success to a mix of luck and persistence rather than being "crushing it" at all times, noting that building a startup is a humbling experience where one often feels like they are "getting their ass kicked."

## Disrupting Venture Capital: The USVC Model
*   **Democratizing Access:** Historically, the SEC’s "accredited investor" laws restricted startup investing to those with a $1M+ net worth. USVC has secured approval to allow anyone to invest in private technology companies with a $500 minimum.
*   **The Goal of Public Ownership:** Nagpal argues that the public narrative around tech and AI is often negative because the average person has no stake in their success. USVC aims to change this by making the "common person" a stakeholder.
*   **Fund Mechanics:**
    *   **Investment Strategy:** The fund invests in direct startup stakes, other venture funds, and SPVs.
    *   **Liquidity:** While venture capital is inherently illiquid, the fund aims to provide quarterly liquidity for up to 5% of the total fund value.
    *   **Net Asset Value (NAV):** Shares are purchased at a current NAV (approximately $20/share), fluctuating based on the valuations of the underlying private holdings.

## Investment Philosophy and Founder Evaluation
*   **Three Pillars of a Great Founder:**
    1.  **Speed of Execution:** High-velocity thinking and acting.
    2.  **Horsepower:** Raw intelligence and a tireless work ethic.
    3.  **Persuasiveness:** The "controversial" ability to convince investors, employees, and customers to believe in a vision.
*   **The "Venture Bargain":** Nagpal warns that most people should *not* raise venture capital. It requires an "irrational" commitment for 10-20 years with a low statistical probability of success. For those seeking a high quality of life, a lifestyle business is often the better path.
*   **Emotional Runway:** Nagpal observed that in the 2021 market downturn, more founders failed because they ran out of "emotional runway" (the will to continue) rather than actual cash in the bank.

## Personal Wealth and Financial Optimizations
*   **The "Happy Number":** For Nagpal, the ideal net worth for lifestyle freedom is roughly $10 million—the point at which one can fly first class, support a family, and eliminate financial stress without needing to be a billionaire.
*   **Portfolio Allocation:** Despite his wealth, Nagpal remains aggressive, with approximately 50% of his portfolio allocated to private startups. He acknowledges this is high-risk and not standard advice for most people.
*   **The Power of Tax Compounding:** He emphasizes that saving $20k in taxes through smart optimization isn't just about the cash—it’s about the millions that those dollars become when invested in the market over a lifetime.

> "Once you’re lucky, twice you’re good. Except I still don’t think I’m very good... running a startup just ends up being a very humbling experience." — Ankur Nagpal

> "Think of venture capital as adventure capital. Do not do this with money you need in any kind of short-term basis." — Ankur Nagpal

> "For almost everyone, you should not raise venture capital... You are effectively signing up to work super hard for a long period of your life with very uncertain reward." — Ankur Nagpal

briefings.title: AI Rally Powers Wall Street Earnings  | Open Interest 5/7/2026
briefings.tldr: Wall Street is flirting with all-time highs fueled by strong corporate earnings and optimism surrounding a proposed deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, even as mixed reports from tech and banking sector guidance flash warning signs about the labor market and consumer sentiment.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
Wall Street is flirting with all-time highs fueled by strong corporate earnings and optimism surrounding a proposed deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, even as mixed reports from tech and banking sector guidance flash warning signs about the labor market and consumer sentiment.

---

## Geopolitical Shifts and Energy Market Impact

* **Strait of Hormuz Negotiations:** The US is awaiting Iran's response via Pakistani mediators regarding a one-page memorandum of understanding. The proposal seeks to gradually reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for lifting the US naval blockade.
* **Oil Prices Retreat:** Brent crude fell below $100 a barrel (down nearly 4%), which helped bonds rally for a second day and fueled equity market optimism. 
* **Oil Trading Investigation:** A series of highly lucrative, well-timed trades executed between March 23 and April 21 has drawn scrutiny. Traders made over $2.6 billion betting that oil prices would drop right before major policy announcements from the US White House and Iran's foreign minister. 
* **Military Stance Remains Active:** Despite active negotiations, the US naval blockade remains firmly in place. CENTCOM confirmed that the US military recently disabled an Iranian-flagged oil tanker attempting to traverse the Gulf of Oman.

## Mixed Corporate Earnings and Growing Consumer Pressures

* **Arm Tumbles on Smartphone Slowdown:** Despite beating fiscal fourth-quarter expectations, Arm shares fell over 8% due to a decline in smartphone shipments. 
    * **The AI Memory Squeeze:** Chipmakers are shifting production away from lower-end consumer electronics (smartphones and PCs) to meet massive demand for memory in AI data centers, inadvertently choking off cheaper consumer hardware segments.
* **Consumer Sector Divergence:**
    * **McDonald's:** EPS topped expectations, but overall sales growth fell short of estimates. Management warned of a meaningful decline in lower-income consumer sentiment heading into Q2, prompting the company to rely heavily on promotional value menus to sustain foot traffic.
    * **Shake Shack and Papa John's:** Both missed revenue estimates as rising food costs (specifically beef prices) squeezed margins. Companies are absorbing these costs internally to prevent a drop in customer volume.
    * **Whirlpool:** Warned of a "recession-level decline" in the appliance sector, indicating that wobbly consumer sentiment is beginning to translate into deferred purchases for big-ticket household goods.
* **IPO Market Resiliency:** Capital markets showed renewed life with two successful, albeit modest, initial public offerings: Hawkeye (satellite location services) and Suja Life (organic beverage brand).

## Wall Street Bonuses, Citigroup's Targets, and Private Capital

* **Citigroup’s Disappointing Outlook:** Citigroup shares fluctuated after the bank set a return on tangible common equity (ROTC) target of 14% to 15% extending all the way out to 2031. Analysts noted this long-term guidance lags significantly behind competitors like Bank of America (16% to 18%) and JPMorgan Chase (which is already printing returns in the 20% range), overshadowing Citi's strong Q1 results and the authorization of a stock buyback program.
* **Rising Banker Compensation:** Wall Street bonuses are projected to rise for a third consecutive year. According to the latest Johnson Associates report, investment bankers in equity underwriting and advisory are poised for the largest payouts on the back of a rebounding deal environment.
* **Private Equity Bottlenecks and Carlyle’s Miss:** Carlyle Group missed quarterly profit estimates despite rising asset sales. The miss was attributed to a technical delay in cash realizations flowing through to shareholders as carried interest.
* **Private Credit Language Shift:** BlackRock reported further markdowns on legacy TCP funds. Due to liquidity concerns, private market players are moving away from the term "semi-liquid" for retail-oriented funds to better align investor expectations with the reality of illiquid assets.

## The AI Capex Boom vs. Labor Market Risks

* **Accelerating S&P Earnings Growth:** S&P 500 earnings growth estimates for the year have surged from an initial 10%–12% up to 20%–27.5%. Bernstein Private Wealth CIO Alex Chaloff noted this growth is highly concentrated in tech and the broader AI ecosystem.
* **Trillion-Dollar Capex Commitments:** Major hyperscalers are implementing five-year infrastructure plans that will deploy trillions of dollars to power AI data centers, which are expected to yield massive long-term productivity gains across the broader economic grid.
* **Labor Market Displacement:** The tech sector is experiencing a persistent trickle of job cuts (e.g., Coinbase, PayPal), with AI increasingly cited as the driver. Chaloff identified the labor market as the "canary in the coal mine" for this economic cycle, as companies seek to replace human overhead with AI systems.
* **Looming Inference Costs:** While companies currently tout massive productivity gains from AI integration, they face a future wave of margin pressure when hyperscalers eventually pass down the currently subsidized, high cost of model inference.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "She's [Jane Fraser] gone from F to C, but the challenge to go from a C grade to an A grade student like some of their peers right now, is a much harder journey, and perhaps their more muted targets that they're setting today is a reflection of that." 
> — *Sridhar Natarajan, on Citigroup's turnaround efforts*

> "This is not a late-cycle corporate environment. The combination of high capex, strong shareholder returns, improving margins, AI-driven productivity, and durable demand is inconsistent with a typical late-cycle slowdown narrative."
> — *Alex Chaloff*

> "Everyone wants memory in their AI data centers, so chipmakers aren't making as much memory for the cheaper goods, like smartphones, like PCs. And so that is hitting a little bit on where they, of course, have huge exposure."
> — *Caroline Hyde, on why chipmaker Arm slid despite record AI demand*

briefings.title: AI dealmaking surges, from roll-ups to Anthropic's compute push — 5/7/2026
briefings.tldr: The AI sector has shifted from experimental technology to a "transformation economy" characterized by the rise of "AI roll-ups" taking legacy public companies private and a fundamental move toward autonomous "agentic engineering" where AI now writes 100% of its own code.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The AI sector has shifted from experimental technology to a "transformation economy" characterized by the rise of "AI roll-ups" taking legacy public companies private and a fundamental move toward autonomous "agentic engineering" where AI now writes 100% of its own code.

## The Rise of the "AI Roll-Up" Strategy
Venture capital firms are moving beyond selling software to enterprises; they are now acquiring legacy service companies outright to implement AI-driven productivity gains internally.

*   **The Long Lake-Amex GBT Deal:** Long Lake, a three-year-old venture-backed company, agreed to take American Express Global Business Travel private for $6.3 billion at a 65% premium. 
    *   **Strategy Focus:** The goal is to apply AI to "non-tech" service industries (healthcare, insurance, property management) that have historically struggled to scale without massive headcount increases.
*   **"Service as Software":** Madhu Namburi (General Catalyst) describes a shift where high-retention service businesses are transformed by AI to drive operating leverage, allowing companies to grow revenue by 20%+ without adding staff.
*   **Nexus Platform:** Long Lake uses a proprietary AI platform to customize models for specialized workflows (e.g., HOA management), reportedly performing 5x better than off-the-shelf models.
*   **Long-Term Outlook:** Long Lake CEO Alex Taubman plans to "own and operate these businesses forever," suggesting that these AI-integrated service companies may eventually return to public markets as a new category of "Applied AI" stocks.

## The Founder Landscape and the "AI Gap"
Morgan Stanley’s inaugural Founders Summit revealed a significant disconnect between the perceived importance of AI and the actual support available for its implementation.

*   **The 23% Support Gap:** While 95% of founders identify AI as critical to their business, only 23% feel supported in its deployment—the widest gap found in the bank’s research.
*   **Operational Challenges:** The struggle is no longer about the technology itself but "operationalizing" it—managing change, integrating it into workflows, and keeping up with the rapid pace of new model releases.
*   **Liquidity Trends:** Despite the abundance of private capital, two-thirds of founders still plan to IPO eventually. However, "secondary" paths (tenders and private share lending) have become mainstream; Morgan Stanley handled $20 billion in tender transactions last year alone.
*   **Founder Performance:** Research confirms that founder-led companies continue to outperform the broader market once public.

## Industrial-Scale Compute and PE Partnerships
The demand for compute is currently exceeding even the most "extreme internal forecasts" at frontier labs, leading to massive new infrastructure deals and private equity vehicles.

*   **SpaceX & Anthropic Deal:** Anthropic announced a massive compute partnership with SpaceX to utilize the Colossus 1 data center in Memphis, bringing 220,000 Nvidia GPUs and 300 megawatts online this month.
*   **Private Equity Shift:** Traditional PE firms are now striking direct deals with AI labs to fund deployment:
    *   **OpenAI:** Launched a $10 billion deployment vehicle with TPG, Brookfield, Advent, and Bain.
    *   **Anthropic:** Formed a $1.5 billion joint venture with Blackstone, Hellman & Friedman, and Goldman Sachs.
*   **Expanding Infrastructure:** This is in addition to Anthropic's existing 5GW partnerships with Amazon and Google, and Microsoft’s $30 billion partnership with Nvidia.

## From "Vibe Code" to Agentic Engineering
Anthropic's development team reports a "phase change" in how software is created, moving toward a world where humans manage autonomous agents.

*   **100% AI-Written Code:** One year ago, 90-95% of Anthropic’s "Claude Code" was written by the model. Today, that figure is 100%. Engineers no longer write source code; they manage agents that manage other agents.
*   **A "Printing Press Moment":** Boris Cherny (Anthropic) compares the current moment to the invention of the printing press, predicting that the democratization of software creation will trigger a new industrial revolution.
*   **Proactive Agents:** New features like "Loops" (scheduling tasks) and "Routines" (event-based responses) allow AI to work autonomously behind the scenes without constant human prompting.
*   **The Evolving Role of Engineers:** The focus for human developers is shifting from syntax and execution to "judgment, taste, and deciding what is worth building."

## Notable Quotes

> "Software, SaaS, the definition was software as a service. I believe it's going to be service as software... the era has come and I think it's going to happen a lot more." — **Madhu Namburi, General Catalyst**

> "We took growth from zero to 5 percent up to over 20 percent revenue growth. When you grow 20 percent... you need more people. Even with the productivity gain, we're creating a lot of jobs." — **Alex Taubman, Long Lake**

> "To me this is like a printing press moment. Everyone is starting to become able to write software in a way that was not the case before... Without reading and writing the Renaissance could not have happened." — **Boris Cherny, Anthropic**

> "The 95 percent point speaks to the consensus that the Fourth Industrial Revolution is here... But the 23 percent who are struggling with it? That's the teething process of moving from being awed by the technology to operationalizing it." — **Mandell Crawley, Morgan Stanley**

briefings.title: AMD Revenue Jumps 38%, Anthropic’s $200B Google Deal, & OpenAI President Greg Brockman on Elon Musk
briefings.tldr: AMD is capitalizing on a massive expansion in the data center CPU market driven by agentic AI inference, while new data reveals a "circular financing" loop where major AI labs like Anthropic commit hundreds of billions in future revenue back to their cloud-provider investors.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
AMD is capitalizing on a massive expansion in the data center CPU market driven by agentic AI inference, while new data reveals a "circular financing" loop where major AI labs like Anthropic commit hundreds of billions in future revenue back to their cloud-provider investors.

## AMD: Shifting from "Share-Taking" to "Share-Grabbing"
* **Financial Performance:** AMD reported a 38% revenue jump to $10.3 billion in Q1, primarily fueled by massive growth in its data center segment.
* **TAM Expansion:** According to Ben Bajarin (CEO of Creative Strategies), the Total Addressable Market (TAM) for CPUs is shifting from a stagnant $25 billion market to a projected $125 billion. 
    * **Agentic Inference:** Unlike traditional cloud workflows, the rise of agentic AI requires significantly more CPU infrastructure, creating "greenfield" growth rather than just stealing market share from Intel.
* **Supply Constraints:** The market is currently in a "compute deficit" where demand outstrips supply so significantly that any viable compute—from Nvidia, AMD, or custom silicon—will find a buyer.
* **Strategic Roadmap:** Investors are looking toward the July "Advancing AI" event for details on the Helios (MI455) system to see if AMD can meaningfully challenge Nvidia’s full-rack dominance.

## The Intertwined Economics of AI Labs and Hyperscalers
* **Anthropic’s $200B Commitment:** New reporting reveals Anthropic has committed approximately $200 billion over five years to Google for computing power and chips.
* **Circular Financing:** A massive portion of hyperscaler revenue backlogs is now tied to the very AI labs they fund.
    * **Google:** Anthropic represents roughly 40% of Google’s $460 billion revenue backlog.
    * **Amazon:** OpenAI and Anthropic are significant contributors to Amazon’s $364 billion backlog.
* **Bubble Concerns:** Industry analysts question if AI is a bubble, noting that much of the reported growth at Google and Microsoft is currently derived from a small handful of AI labs (OpenAI and Anthropic) rather than broad enterprise adoption.
* **Oracle’s Unique Position:** Unlike the other hyperscalers who resell models, Oracle is focused on building physical data center infrastructure specifically for OpenAI, a deal valued at roughly $300 billion.

## Musk v. OpenAI: Testimony from Greg Brockman
* **Elon Musk’s AI Intuition:** OpenAI President Greg Brockman testified that Musk was initially unimpressed by the technology that became ChatGPT, calling it "stupid" and suggesting kids on the internet could do a better job.
* **The "Morally Bankrupt" Memo:** Brockman addressed a digital journal entry where he contemplated a "morally bankrupt" path; he clarified this referred to a plan to fire Musk and start a for-profit without him—a path the company ultimately did not take.
* **Tesla Collaboration:** In a contrasting anecdote, Brockman noted that co-founder Ilya Sutskever previously assisted Tesla’s self-driving efforts, providing the insight that specific data collection (10,000 images of poor road conditions) would solve their AI hurdles.

## Enterprise Adoption and the Chatbot Race
* **Tessera Labs Funding:** The company raised $60 million in a round led by Andreessen Horowitz. 
    * **Focus:** CEO Kabir Nagrecha noted the firm uses AI to automate "heavy legacy" IT work, such as ERP migrations and on-prem-to-cloud transitions, which often act as bottlenecks to AI adoption.
* **Subscriber Survey Results:** A survey of 574 *The Information* subscribers indicates a tightening race among AI chat services:
    * **Claude:** 60% usage (taking the lead).
    * **ChatGPT:** 57% usage.
    * **Gemini:** 56% usage.
* **Tool Trends:** While ChatGPT's early lead is eroding, usage of advanced tools like coding assistants is rising, though established names like GitHub Copilot saw slight declines in this specific cohort.

> "We’re at such a compute deficit for AI that the reality is almost any viable compute will get adopted... You need two, you need three, you may even need four vendors to have enough to meet this demand." — **Ben Bajarin**, CEO of Creative Strategies

> "Oftentimes this AI transition and moving to AI usage is gatekept and bottlenecked behind making that first digital transformation... our view is bringing AI into that journey to solve the prerequisites for AI." — **Kabir Nagrecha**, CEO of Tessera Labs

> "Brockman said he doesn't think Elon is very good at AI. He said he knows cars, he knows rockets, sure, but he doesn't know too much about AI." — **Rocket Drew**, Reporter at The Information

briefings.title: Are UFOs Actually Demons in Disguise?

people.name: JD Vance
people.role: Vice President of the United States

briefings.tldr: Modern UFO phenomena are increasingly viewed through a religious and "preternatural" lens by both scholars and high-level government officials, bridging the gap between physical evidence and metaphysical experience.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Modern UFO phenomena are increasingly viewed through a religious and "preternatural" lens by both scholars and high-level government officials, bridging the gap between physical evidence and metaphysical experience.

## The Intersection of UFOs and Religious Theology
*   **The "Preternatural" Category:** Dr. Diana Pasulka explains that Catholicism maintains a specific category for non-human intelligence—the "preternatural"—which encompasses entities like angels or fallen angels that are distinct from both the natural world and the divine supernatural.
*   **A New Form of Religiosity:** Pasulka views modern UFO reports as a continuation of historical supernatural encounters, such as the Virgin Mary apparitions or Irish folklore regarding fairies.
*   **Jacques Vallée’s Influence:** The discussion highlights the work of computer scientist Jacques Vallée, who theorized that UFO sightings are part of a persistent human tradition of interacting with "other" beings that do not appear fully human.
*   **Religious Frameworks:** Pasulka argues that if society is on the verge of acknowledging non-human intelligence, traditional religion provides the most established "organic framework" for humans to interface with such entities.

## Government Interest and the "Disclosure" Movement
*   **High-Level Political Engagement:** Ross Douthat notes that traditionally sober, "headline-avoidant" politicians like Senator Mike Rounds and Senator Chuck Schumer have shown a strange, persistent interest in UFO data collection and disclosure.
*   **The AATIP Catalyst:** The 2017 "Tic Tac" video release was the result of a $22 million defense budget provision secured by the late Senator Harry Reid.
    *   Douthat notes the skepticism surrounding this: some argue the government "psy-oped" itself into belief because Reid funded a specific group of enthusiasts within the bureaucracy.
*   **Presidential Rhetoric:** The speakers discuss the "weird" language used by Donald Trump and Barack Obama regarding classified information on UFOs, suggesting the government may be "tap dancing" around a reality they don't fully understand.
*   **Skepticism of Full Disclosure:** Both guests express doubt that any upcoming government "disclosure" will provide a "smoking gun," with Douthat predicting it will likely follow the pattern of the JFK files—lots of "light" but little "heat."

## Physical Evidence and Crash Retrievals
*   **The "Metallic Frog Skin":** Pasulka recounts a 2012 expedition to a New Mexico "crash site" with Stanford scientist Garry Nolan (referred to as "Tyler" in her book *American Cosmic*).
    *   They recovered debris that Nolan later claimed was "engineered" at a level impossible for the era it was allegedly found (the 1940s).
*   **Crash Retrieval Programs:** While "crash retrieval" is a standard military function for fallen satellites or foreign drones, Pasulka asserts that a subset of these programs specifically focuses on unidentified objects.
*   **The Disinformation Theory:** A competing narrative (recently highlighted by the *Wall Street Journal*) suggests that the entire UFO movement is a government-run disinformation campaign designed to hide advanced U.S. aerospace technology.
    *   Douthat finds this theory plausible for government interest but notes it fails to explain historical "encounter narratives," such as the 1994 Ariel School sighting in Zimbabwe.

## Expert Perspectives on Key Figures
*   **David Grusch:** Both guests describe the high-profile whistleblower as "frustrating," largely due to the extraordinary nature of his claims (such as the Vatican being involved in a 1930s UFO recovery) coupled with a lack of public evidence.
*   **Sean Kirkpatrick:** Former head of AARO (All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office), Kirkpatrick has criticized the UFO movement as a "faith-based" system that has "seeped into the highest levels of government" without empirical proof.
*   **Leslie Kean:** Pasulka cites the investigative journalist who co-wrote the 2017 *New York Times* UFO expose as the researcher she respects the most in the field.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "I think there are ways in which elements of the UFO phenomena look like sort of characteristic but at the same time extremely bizarre forms of spiritual and supernatural experience... that would fit pretty comfortably inside a kind of William James style account of the varieties of religious experience." — **Ross Douthat**

> "The Catholic Church... has a well-formed category for understanding non-human intelligence, be it extraterrestrial or interdimensional. And this is called the preternatural... things that are not necessarily from God, but are in between." — **Dr. Diana Pasulka**

> "The strange thing about the last five or ten years is that a lot of people inside the government... have acted like there is something a little bit more objective associated with this, that it’s not just something you would analyze in terms of people’s subjective experiences." — **Ross Douthat**

> "If indeed it's the case that we are on the dawn of learning about non-human intelligence, the organic framework that we already have is religion. Traditional religions have already helped us learn to interface with non-human intelligence." — **Dr. Diana Pasulka**

briefings.title: Boston Fed President Collins on FOMC Dissent and Kevin Warsh’s Nomination | Big Take
briefings.tldr: Boston Fed President Susan Collins supports the recent shift toward policy dissent, arguing against an "easing bias" as the war in Iran and persistent supply shocks delay inflation's return to the 2% target.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Boston Fed President Susan Collins supports the recent shift toward policy dissent, arguing against an "easing bias" as the war in Iran and persistent supply shocks delay inflation's return to the 2% target. As the Fed prepares for leadership under nominee Kevin Warsh, officials are bracing for potential "regime change" and structural reforms to the central bank’s communication and modeling.

## FOMC Dissent and Policy Stance
* **Historical Dissent:** The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) recently saw an 8-4 vote to hold rates steady, the highest level of disagreement since 1992.
    * **The "Easing Bias" Conflict:** While Collins (a non-voter this year) supported holding rates, she sided with dissenters Laurie Logan, Beth Hammack, and Neel Kashkari, who opposed statement language implying the next move would likely be a rate cut.
    * **Diverse Perspectives:** One member, Steven Myron, dissented in favor of a quarter-point cut, illustrating a widening range of views on the committee.
* **Consensus vs. Unanimity:** Collins emphasized that "consensus" does not mean "unanimity." She views the current lack of a unified front as a healthy reflection of economic uncertainty rather than a breakdown in leadership.

## Inflation Outlook and the Impact of Conflict
* **War in Iran:** Collins identifies the conflict as a primary driver of renewed inflationary risk.
    * **Price Surges:** Baseline expectations for disinflation have been pushed further out due to surges in energy and food prices.
    * **1973 Comparison:** Collins noted that while the current energy shock is of a similar magnitude to the 1973 oil shock, the U.S. is better positioned today as a net oil exporter.
* **Inflation Projections:** Collins expects core inflation to remain elevated, likely ending the year around 3%.
    * **Credibility Concerns:** She expressed concern over the Fed’s credibility, noting the 2% inflation target has been missed for over five years.
    * **Expectations:** There is an increased risk that longer-term inflation expectations could become "unanchored" if the Fed does not demonstrate a firm commitment to its target.

## State of the Labor Market and Economy
* **Resilient Growth:** Despite global shocks, the U.S. economy remains surprisingly resilient with strong investment and a rebound in consumption.
* **The "Unusual Balance":** Collins describes the labor market as stable but containing pockets of fragility.
    * **Employment Data:** The unemployment rate has held at approximately 4.3% for several months.
    * **Warning Signs:** Concerns remain regarding high duration of unemployment and elevated jobless rates among college-age and younger workers.
* **Supply Chain "New Normal":** The Fed is monitoring a series of supply shocks (Pandemic, Russia-Ukraine, tariffs, and Iran). However, Collins noted that productivity gains have acted as a "positive supply shock" that supports growth while dampening inflation.

## Leadership Transition: Jerome Powell to Kevin Warsh
* **The Warsh Nomination:** Kevin Warsh is expected to be confirmed as the 17th Fed Chair by the June 16th meeting. 
    * **Regime Change:** Warsh has signaled a desire for "big reforms," including potential changes to how the Fed communicates with markets, uses forward guidance, and models inflation.
    * **Independence:** Collins indicated she is taking Warsh’s public comments regarding Fed independence "at face value" but remains cautious about the specific details of his reform agenda.
* **Powell’s Continued Presence:** In a rare move, Jerome Powell intends to remain on the Fed’s Board of Governors after his term as Chair ends, a decision that has drawn political scrutiny but may provide a counterweight during the transition.

> "My preference also would have been to adjust the statement to... not be as closely aligned with language that has been associated with the presumption that the next move will be a cut." — **Susan Collins**

> "I am concerned about... the credibility of having a 2% target that we have missed now for over five years... If inflation expectations were to become unanchored, that would complicate the task that Congress has set for us." — **Susan Collins**

> "The labor market in my view does seem to be in balance, even though it's an unusual balance... The unemployment rate has been at around 4.3% now for a number of months." — **Susan Collins**

briefings.title: Brazil's Lula Reveals Key Details of Meeting With Trump – Trade Deals, Tariffs & Cooperation | AC1N
briefings.tldr: President Lula and President Trump have established a high-level working group with a 30-day deadline to resolve trade and tariff disputes, while signaling a renewed strategic partnership centered on critical minerals, infrastructure investment, and global security.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
President Lula and President Trump have established a high-level working group with a 30-day deadline to resolve trade and tariff disputes, while signaling a renewed strategic partnership centered on critical minerals, infrastructure investment, and global security.

## Trade and Economic Recalibration
*   **Tariff Resolution:** President Lula proposed a 30-day "hammer-down" deadline for trade officials to resolve disputes regarding import taxes and tariffs, aiming to bypass bureaucratic inertia.
    *   Lula noted that despite perceptions of high Brazilian taxes, the average tax on U.S. goods is 2.7%, though some specific products hit 12%.
    *   Brazil currently faces a $14 billion trade deficit with the U.S. and seeks to rebalance the relationship after decades of U.S. trade hegemony being eroded by China.
*   **U.S. Reinvestment:** Lula urged the U.S. to return its focus to Latin American infrastructure, noting that Chinese firms often dominate international tenders for Brazilian roads and railways because the U.S. fails to participate.
*   **Data Centers:** Brazil is open to hosting international data centers provided the companies finance their own energy production, ensuring Brazil’s power grid is not strained for foreign data storage.

## Strategic Resources and National Sovereignty
*   **Critical Minerals:** Lula highlighted new Brazilian legislation that treats critical minerals as a matter of national sovereignty while inviting international partnerships.
    *   Brazil has only mapped 30% of its territory for minerals and intends to reach 100% via partnerships with the U.S., China, Germany, and others.
    *   The goal is to move beyond raw extraction toward domestic processing and wealth creation.
*   **Energy Transition:** Lula positioned Brazil as a global leader in energy transition, inviting U.S. entrepreneurship to participate in green energy projects.

## Organized Crime and Public Security
*   **Economic Alternatives:** Lula argued that military bases alone cannot stop the drug trade; the international community must provide economic alternatives for farmers to replace illicit crops with profitable, legal agriculture.
*   **Global Task Force:** Brazil proposed a multilateral working group to share expertise in combating organized crime.
    *   **Focus Areas:** Lula emphasized the need to tackle the financial infrastructure of gangs, weapon smuggling (noting many arms in Brazil originate in the U.S.), and money laundering within U.S. states.
*   **Domestic Security:** Brazil plans to launch a comprehensive national plan against organized crime next week, focusing on reclaiming territories from criminal factions.

## Global Diplomacy and Geopolitics
*   **UN Reform:** Lula pressed Trump on the need to reform the UN Security Council, advocating for permanent seats for nations like Brazil, India, Mexico, and representatives from Africa to reflect the "2026 geopolitics" rather than the 1945 status quo.
*   **Dialogue vs. Conflict:** Lula reiterated his preference for narrative and dialogue over war, specifically mentioning concerns regarding the invasion of Iran and the protracted conflict between Russia and Ukraine.
*   **Bilateral Rapport:** Despite past political differences, Lula described a "chemistry" and "love at first sight" relationship with Trump, emphasizing that democratic stability in the two largest Western Hemisphere nations serves as a global example.
*   **Non-Interference:** Lula dismissed concerns about U.S. interference in Brazilian domestic politics or the 2026 election, stating that the Brazilian people—and only the Brazilian people—decide their destiny.

## Notable Quotes

> "The public machine is eternal, but the president has an expiration date. We have a four-year mandate; things have to happen. We must establish goal plans so people deliver what society expects of us." — **President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva**

> "I told President Trump that it is important for the United States to have interest in Brazil's things again. For example, we often hold international tenders for a highway or railroad, and the U.S. doesn't participate. The Chinese do." — **President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva**

> "I believe much more in dialogue than in war. We know how a war begins, but no one knows how it ends. That is why talking is much cheaper and more effective." — **President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva**

> "The only things we do not give up are our democracy and our sovereignty. Everything else is debatable." — **President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva**

briefings.title: Brookfield's Bruce Flatt discusses the global markets at the Milken Institute Global Conference
briefings.tldr: The global economy is entering a $10 trillion "rewiring" phase driven by AI and digital infrastructure needs, shifting the investment landscape from traditional assets to long-term "continuity" assets managed by private capital firms rather than debt-constrained governments.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The global economy is entering a $10 trillion "rewiring" phase driven by AI and digital infrastructure needs, shifting the investment landscape from traditional assets to long-term "continuity" assets managed by private capital firms rather than debt-constrained governments.

## The $10 Trillion Infrastructure "Rewiring"
*   **Scale of Investment:** Bruce Flatt (CEO, Brookfield) estimates a $10 trillion global expenditure over the next decade to build out power grids, AI factories, data centers, and fiber networks. 
*   **Infrastructure Pivot:** The global economy is transitioning from legacy networks (highways and railways) to a digital backbone. 50% of the assets Brookfield owns today did not exist as investable asset classes 15 years ago.
*   **Supply Shortages vs. AI Bubble:** Larry Fink (CEO, BlackRock) argues that we are in a supply shortage rather than a bubble. The U.S. is currently short on power, compute capacity, chips, and memory. 
*   **New Security Paradigms:** The rise of drone warfare is necessitating a reevaluation of physical security for infrastructure, potentially moving critical $50B–$75B data center investments underground to protect against domestic and international threats.

## Stability and the Private Capital Advantage
*   **Asset-Liability Matching:** Michael Milken highlighted that recent bank failures (Silicon Valley Bank, First Republic) resulted from mismatched liabilities. In contrast, both Brookfield and BlackRock report that less than 1% of their managed assets are redeemable on a quarterly basis.
*   **The Role of Private Markets:** With governments facing mounting deficits, the private sector is now the primary engine for massive infrastructure builds. Long-term private capital acts as a stable intermediary that the two-year capital structure of the banking system cannot support.
*   **Solution-Based Investing:** Large firms are moving away from selling "products" and toward "solutions." This includes bespoke vehicles, such as one mentioned by Flatt that locks in capital for 27 years to match long-tail institutional liabilities.

## Global Market Democratization and Retirement
*   **Shift to Self-Directed Retirement:** BlackRock is working with countries like Saudi Arabia and India to move away from government-sponsored pensions toward personal, defined-contribution plans.
*   **The Japanese Catalyst:** Fink noted that the Japanese stock market's recent surge was directly tied to the doubling of tax exemptions for "NISA" (self-directed retirement accounts), proving that domestic capital participation drives market valuation.
*   **Wages vs. Capital:** Fink warns that in an AI-driven world, wages will not keep pace with the growth of capital. Broad economic success now requires getting individual citizens to invest in capital markets rather than keeping money in low-interest bank accounts.

## The Strategy of Long-Term Compounding
*   **The "Miracle" of 12%:** Bruce Flatt emphasized that consistent 12% compounding over long periods is more valuable than chasing volatile 35% returns. The goal is to own "great businesses" for decades rather than churning assets.
*   **Consolidation of Winners:** The panel predicted a "K-shaped" economy where one or two winners dominate each industry due to the massive CAPEX required to integrate AI. 
*   **Institutional Scale:** The era of $100 billion funds is ending; the market is moving toward a landscape of 30+ funds managing over $1 trillion each. These "mega-funds" require "continuity assets" they can hold indefinitely to avoid the friction of constant asset churning.

## Notable Quotes
> "We are rewiring the global economy to lay the networks that we laid before, which were highways, utilities, railways. And now we're laying cloud, artificial intelligence factories, and data centers." — **Bruce Flatt, CEO of Brookfield Corporation**

> "There is not an AI bubble. There is the opposite. We have supply shortages. Demand is growing much faster than anyone had ever anticipated." — **Larry Fink, CEO of BlackRock**

> "Having your money in a bank account is one of the worst financial decisions of a lifetime... we are not going to be able to broaden economic success only by wages because wages in this AI world are not going to grow as fast as the potential of the AI growth." — **Larry Fink, CEO of BlackRock**

> "The greatest miracle of investing, finance, in fact, almost everything, is compounding... if you can earn north of 12%, nothing else matters. Don't try to earn 35%." — **Bruce Flatt, CEO of Brookfield Corporation**

briefings.title: Build your AI Muscle 💪❗️| Keynote @qsummit Startup Conference
briefings.tldr: We are in a 1,000-day window of fundamental economic and educational transformation where AI agents and "personal tutors" allow for hyper-lean, billion-dollar scale.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
We are in a 1,000-day window of fundamental economic and educational transformation where AI agents and "personal tutors" allow for hyper-lean, billion-dollar scale. Success in this era requires a shift from passive social media consumption to a daily practice of "building AI muscle" through hands-on experimentation.

## The New Economic Reality: The Rise of the "N-of-1" Giant
* **Hyper-Lean Scaling:** The era of the one- or two-person billion-dollar company has arrived.
    * **Example:** Matthew Gallagher’s company generates $1.8 billion in sales with only one employee, managing everything else through AI tools like Claude and Gemini.
* **The 1,000-Day Window:** Former Stability AI CEO Emad Mostaque posits that we are in a 1,000-day cycle where economics will change fundamentally.
* **The Shift to Agentic AI:** Estimates suggest agentic AI (autonomous agents) will own 60% of software economics by 2030, though it will likely happen much sooner.
* **Internal Disruption:** Daniel Jung revealed he transitioned his own business from a team of 12 employees to a model run entirely by himself and AI, significantly reducing costs while increasing reach.

## The Evolution of Learning: Solving the "2 Sigma Problem"
* **Personal AI Tutors:** The "2 Sigma problem"—the idea that students with 1-on-1 tutors perform two standard deviations better—is effectively solved. Anyone can now build a "Jarvis-style" tutor in their pocket.
* **RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation):** To avoid AI hallucinations in education, Jung emphasizes RAG pipelines.
    * By training AI on specific, trusted datasets (like his own 3,000+ math videos and scripts), he creates tutors that provide 100% accurate, curated answers with source citations.
* **Meta-Skill Mastery:** Nobel Prize winner Demis Hassabis (Google DeepMind) emphasizes that "learning how to learn" is the only vital skill for the next decade of rapid change.
* **Evidence-Based Success:** Harvard studies show that AI tutoring now outperforms traditional active learning methods in subjects like physics.

## Building "AI Muscle": From Consumption to Action
* **The Daily AI Ritual:** Jung urges a commitment of 30 to 90 minutes every day to learn AI tools. 
    * This isn't "nerd stuff" anymore; it is the new literacy.
* **The "Do, Learn, Repeat" Framework:** Move away from theoretical learning to "Action Mode."
    * **Tool Spotlight:** **NotebookLM** is cited as "the best tool on earth" for grounding AI in specific PDFs and podcasts to create summaries, quizzes, and personalized study guides.
    * **Automation:** Tools like **n8n** allow for drag-and-drop workflow automation, enabling users to build complex systems without deep coding knowledge.
* **Algorithm Curation:** Jung recommends creating new, clean social media accounts (TikTok/Instagram) dedicated solely to training the algorithm on AI news and experts to eliminate distraction.

## Global Scaling via Personal Branding
* **Global Reach without Language Barriers:** Jung is currently scaling his brand toward "1 billion views" by using AI agents to dub his math content into English, Portuguese, and Spanish.
    * The process is entirely automated; he does not speak the languages, yet the AI maintains his voice and persona.
* **The Trust Factor:** As deepfakes become indistinguishable from reality, the value of a trusted "Personal Brand" increases. AI should be used to empower the human element, not replace the need for trust.

## Notable Quotes

> "The greatest shortcoming of the human race is our inability to understand the exponential function... if you double your steps 30 times, you land nearly two times to the moon and back. This is the time we are in." — **Daniel Jung**

> "Learning to learn is the key skill. The only thing we know for sure is it’s going to be a lot of change over the next 10 years." — **Demis Hassabis** (Founder, Google DeepMind)

> "I’m running my company with no persons now. I had 12 employees; everything is running on AI. For me, it’s a cost-saver and a time-saver." — **Daniel Jung**

> "Don’t quit university, but if you deal with [AI] in the best case, you earn a lot of money... it is your turn now. Wake up your inner child and build your AI muscle." — **Daniel Jung**

briefings.title: Demis Hassabis on AGI, Robots Scale Production, and Elon’s $1T Mars-Shot Comp | EP 253
briefings.tldr: At a special Moonshots panel at MIT, Peter H. Diamandis and exponential technology experts analyzed the rapid scaling of humanoid robotics, the legal battle over OpenAI's corporate governance, and a future where AI-driven scientific discovery and advanced biotechnology reshape global economics and human biology.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
At a special Moonshots panel at MIT, Peter H. Diamandis and exponential technology experts analyzed the rapid scaling of humanoid robotics, the legal battle over OpenAI's corporate governance, and a future where AI-driven scientific discovery and advanced biotechnology reshape global economics and human biology.

***

## The Frontier of AGI and the OpenAI Legal Battle

* **Elon Musk’s $500B Mars-Shot Compensation:** The panel discussed the unprecedented SpaceX board compensation package designed for Elon Musk, featuring 200 million super-voting shares (10-to-1 voting power) unlocked only upon hitting a 1-million-person Mars colony and a $7.5 trillion market valuation.
    * **Corporate Governance:** Dave Blundin noted that super-voting shares lock in visionary founders to pursue "crazy-sounding" ideas that traditional, risk-averse boards would block.
    * **Space Compute:** The package also grants Musk 60.4 million restricted shares when SpaceX brings online 100 terawatts of space compute.
* **Musk v. OpenAI Lawsuit:** Elon Musk's lawsuit seeks $150 billion in damages, the reversion of OpenAI to non-profit status, and the removal of Sam Altman and Greg Brockman. 
    * **The "Smoking Gun" Diary:** The trial revealed Greg Brockman’s diary entries, which noted, *"We truly want the B Corp. The true answer is that we want Elon out... Can't see us turning this into a for-profit without a nasty fight."*
    * **Legal Vulnerabilities:** On the defense side, emails from 2017 showed Musk’s own team negotiating for equity in a transition to a for-profit entity, and Musk admitted that xAI has distilled its models from OpenAI's data.
* **Has AGI Already Arrived?:** DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis recently stated that achieving AGI may not require a major breakthrough, relying instead on the success of foundation models. 
    * **The 2020 Benchmark:** Alex Wisner-Gross argued that true AGI was effectively achieved in the summer of 2020 with the publication of the GPT-3 paper, which proved that general intelligence could be reached by compressing general human knowledge.
    * **The Counter-Argument:** Co-author Steven Kotler strongly disputed this, arguing that current AI is merely a "convergent thinking engine" that fails at creative divergence and remains a highly limited writing and scientific tool.

## Humanoid Robotics and Manufacturing Scale-Up

* **Figure AI’s Production Surge:** Figure AI (led by Brett Adcock) has successfully scaled its manufacturing capabilities from producing one humanoid robot per day to one robot per hour, with a target of 100,000 robots by 2030.
* **1X Technologies:** The robotics company is targeting a production goal of 10,000 "Neo" humanoid robots this year and 100,000 by 2027 out of their new 58,000-square-foot facility in Hawthorne, California.
* **The 10-Billion-Robot Prediction:** Panelists evaluated projections from both Elon Musk and Brett Adcock that the world will see up to 10 billion humanoid robots by 2040. 
    * **Eldercare and Labor:** Humanoid form factors will be vital to navigate physical infrastructure built for humans, especially as demographic decline leaves nations with shrinking labor pools.
    * **Post-Humanoid Form Factors:** Alex Wisner-Gross predicted that by 2040, exotic shapes—such as micro-scale nanorobots—will make traditional humanoid form factors look "prosaic," with trillions of nanorobots operating across the solar system.

## The "Singularity Economy": China's Labor Safeguards & Biotech 

* **China’s AI Employment Rulings:** In a landmark case in Hangzhou, a Chinese court ruled that a company cannot demote or fire an employee simply because AI can perform their tasks more cheaply. The court reasoned that adopting AI is a voluntary business choice, not an unavoidable external shock that invalidates an employment contract.
* **GLP-1 Drugs Outperforming AI Revenue:** Dual-acting and single peptide weight-loss drugs (like Ozempic and Mounjaro) generated more revenue in 2025 than OpenAI and Anthropic combined by a factor of 2.4. 
    * **Healthspan vs. AI Labor:** The panel framed this as an economic race between investing in biological human healthspan (maximizing human labor) versus digital AI labor.
* **Retatrutide as "Biotech AGI":** Eli Lilly’s upcoming triple-agonist peptide, Retatrutide, is showing unprecedented clinical results, including a 37-pound average weight loss over 40 weeks, a 27% drop in cholesterol, and an 80% reduction in liver fat. Salim Ismail shared that he has used Retatrutide to successfully reverse decades of liver damage.

## What AI Will Feel Like by Mid-2028

* **Omnipresent "Ambient" AI:** Peter Diamandis predicted that consumers will transition to "ambient AI," giving models permission to listen to all phone calls, track health vitals, and read emails to create a highly optimized, frictionless daily existence.
* **Hardware Bottlenecks:** Despite the demand for consumer AI, Dave Blundin warned that a severe global shortfall in compute and data center capacity will limit the availability of top-tier models to everyday consumers by 2028, as enterprise players monopolize the supply.
* **Cognitive Merging:** Looking further ahead, Wisner-Gross noted that extrapolating the physical shrinkage of a gigaflop of compute suggests that by the mid-2040s, a computer capable of advanced AI processing will be the size of a human eukaryotic cell, enabling true biological integration.

***

## Notable Quotes

> "We realized as a civilization, certainly no later than 2020, that you could carry out a diverse and general range of tasks with models that had compressed human knowledge. That’s all that we needed. Everything else... is just incremental improvements."
> — *Alex Wisner-Gross*

> "My daily experience... as a writer is, this machine doesn't know shit. I spend more time trying to teach it how to write than watching it write... This is a convergent thinking engine, it doesn't do divergence, and most of the creative breakthroughs [require divergence]."
> — *Steven Kotler*

> "We need to rewrite the operating system for civilization, because everything we've done as a civilization, every business in the world for 10,000 years, is trying to solve scarcity. And now we're moving into an era of abundance."
> — *Salim Ismail*

> "Right now, we've lived this beautiful moment in time where the very best foundation models are made available to anyone on the planet... near free. You got to take advantage of this moment in time because it's going to get really bottlenecked by 2028."
> — *Dave Blundin*

briefings.title: EARNINGS ALERT: TTD, CRWV, COIN
briefings.tldr: Post-market trading saw a sharp sell-off in major tech and ad-tech names as Trade Desk and Cloudflare plummeted on disappointing guidance and margin compression, overshadowing a massive $100 billion backlog report from AI-infrastructure provider CoreWeave.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Post-market trading saw a sharp sell-off in major tech and ad-tech names as Trade Desk and Cloudflare plummeted on disappointing guidance and margin compression, overshadowing a massive $100 billion backlog report from AI-infrastructure provider CoreWeave.

## The Trade Desk (TTD): Decelerating Growth and Executive Turnover
*   **Market Reaction:** Shares dropped approximately 15% in after-hours trading following a mixed report and weak forward guidance.
*   **Financial Performance:**
    *   **Earnings Miss:** Adjusted EPS came in at $0.28, missing the $0.32 consensus estimate.
    *   **Revenue Beat:** First-quarter revenue hit $689 million, slightly exceeding the $679.5 million expected.
*   **Outlook Concerns:**
    *   **Guidance Shortfall:** Q2 revenue guidance of $750 million fell short of the $772.4 million street estimate.
    *   **Margin Compression:** Adjusted EBITDA margins narrowed to 30%, down from 34% in the same period last year.
*   **Strategic Headwinds:**
    *   **Leadership Exit:** The Chief Strategy Officer is departing to join OpenAI, adding to investor uncertainty.
    *   **Competitive Pressure:** Analysts noted increasing competition from "walled garden" giants like Google, Meta, and Amazon.
    *   **Potential Tailwinds:** Some analysts (Wedbush) suggest upcoming FIFA World Cup and political ad spending could provide a summer boost.

## CoreWeave (CRWV): Massive AI Backlog Amidst Heavy Spending
*   **Backlog Growth:** The company reported a massive revenue backlog (RPO) of $100 billion, up from $67 billion in the previous quarter, driven by deals with Meta and Anthropic.
*   **Mixed Financials:**
    *   **Revenue:** Beat expectations at $2.08 billion (vs. $1.97 billion estimate).
    *   **Profitability:** Reported a wider-than-expected net loss of $740 million ($1.40 per share).
*   **Operational Scaling:**
    *   **Power Capacity:** Management aims to surpass 1 gigawatt of active power soon, with a long-term goal of 8 gigawatts by 2030.
    *   **Business Model:** Functioning as a "neo-cloud," CoreWeave services the compute overflow that major hyperscalers like AWS or Google cannot currently handle.

## Cloudflare (NET): Valuation "Rug Pull" and Workforce Trimming
*   **Stock Plummet:** Shares fell 12–15% despite raising full-year EPS guidance, as investors balked at the company's high valuation multiples.
*   **Margin Miss:** Gross margins came in at 72.8%, missing the 75% target, which analyst George Tsilis identified as a primary concern for the "momentum chasers."
*   **Labor Shift:** The company announced a workforce reduction of approximately 1,100 employees to optimize the current structure.
*   **Comparison:** In contrast, competitor Akamai (AKAM) saw shares surge 24% after hours, as investors pivoted toward more reasonably valued names in the content delivery space.

## Coinbase (COIN): Persistent Cash Burn and Transaction Lag
*   **Revenue Miss:** Q1 revenue of $1.4 billion missed the $1.5 billion estimate, leading to a 3% decline in share price.
*   **Financial Health:**
    *   **Net Loss:** The company reported a net loss of $394.1 million for the quarter.
    *   **Subscription Weakness:** Q2 subscription and services revenue guidance ($565M–$645M) was entirely below street expectations.
*   **Growth Strategy:** Management is pivoting toward derivatives trading via their "Everything Exchange" to offset slowing spot crypto trading volumes.

> **KG (Analyst):** "We don't have a bottom yet when it comes to the fundamentals for [The Trade Desk]... the revenue growth is still decelerating. I'm not sure the CEO is showing any type of results when it comes to profitability or taking market share."

> **George Tsilis:** "The challenge with [Cloudflare] is the valuation... effectively going into this the stock was already expensive on an earnings basis... right now there's a bit of a rug pull happening because it was just not enough."

> **Sam (Schwab Network):** "The market is very sensitive to the level of spending here... there's a view that they need to be showing that they've got supporting revenue growth."

briefings.title: EP301. PLTR 會被打敗嗎、SpaceXAI 算力出租中、輝達台北 GTC | M觀點
briefings.tldr: Palantir 憑藉其「追求 Alpha」的企業文化與完整的責任鏈體系，在企業核心決策領域難以被「管顧公司 + AI 模型」的組合擊敗；與此同時，AI 市場正轉向實體 AI 應用與算力租賃的新階段。
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**  
Palantir 憑藉其「追求 Alpha」的企業文化與完整的責任鏈體系，在企業核心決策領域難以被「管顧公司 + AI 模型」的組合擊敗；與此同時，AI 市場正轉向實體 AI 應用與算力租賃的新階段。

## Palantir 的競爭優勢與市場定位
* **信任鏈與責任鏈：** Palantir 提供的是端到端的整合服務。
    * 相較於 OpenAI 或 Anthropic 需透過管顧公司導入，Palantir 避開了「雙頭馬車」的利益衝突，能將產品回饋直接轉化為系統改良，而非讓價值流失在諮詢服務中。
* **「Alpha」企業文化：** Palantir 核心價值在於追求非對稱優勢（Alpha）。
    * **文化差異：** 大多數模型公司與管顧公司傾向提供「Beta」（標準、合理的現有知識），而 Palantir 則像 SpaceX，致力於推翻現狀做最頂尖的決策系統。
* **市場份額預測：** Palantir 並非要吞下整個市場。
    * 主持人認為 Palantir 專攻利潤最高、最頂尖的 10% 企業市場；剩下 90% 的中小企業市場將由微軟（Work IQ）、OpenAI 及 Anthropic 分割。

## 算力租賃市場：xAI 與 Anthropic 的合作
* **Anthropic 的算力荒：** 由於第一季表現強勁，Anthropic 目前面臨算力不足導致模型表現受限及客戶流失（約 10-20% 轉向 OpenAI）。
* **SpaceXAI（xAI）的角色：** 馬斯克利用旗下的資料中心提供「及時雨」。
    * **Colossus 2 資料中心：** 部署超過 50 萬張 GB200/GB300 顯卡。
    * **效能提升：** Colossus 2 的總算力預估是 Colossus 1 的 5 到 10 倍，在滿足自家 Grok 模型訓練之餘，有餘力高價轉租給 Anthropic。

## 輝達台北 GTC：企業導入 AI 的關鍵趨勢
* **Token 經濟學（Token Economics）：** 投資人應關注「每瓦 Token 產出數」與「Token 成本」。
    * 這是未來輝達 GPU 與各家 ASIC 晶片競爭的勝負關鍵，決定了 AI 工廠的營運效率。
* **長時間運行代理（Long-running AI Agents）：** AI 不再只是回答問題，而是能長時間執行複雜工作流的代理人，將成為企業流程突破的下一個重點。
* **實體 AI 與機器人協作：** 未來的智慧工廠將由「通用型機器人（人型）」與「專用型機器人（機械手臂）」協同作業，而非單一方案。

## 產業應用實例：醫療與製造業
* **智慧醫療（鴻海）：** 推出 NeuroBot 半人型醫療機器人。

briefings.title: Epstein Files News LIVE: Howard Lutnick Faces Closed-Door Grilling By House Oversight Committee
briefings.tldr: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick faced a four-and-a-half-hour closed-door grilling by the House Oversight Committee regarding contradictions between his public statements and his documented history with Jeffrey Epstein, while a federal judge unsealed a 2019 suicide note from Epstein’s initial failed attempt.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick faced a four-and-a-half-hour closed-door grilling by the House Oversight Committee regarding contradictions between his public statements and his documented history with Jeffrey Epstein, while a federal judge unsealed a 2019 suicide note from Epstein’s initial failed attempt.

## Lutnick’s Testimony and Ties to Jeffrey Epstein
* **Contradictory Statements:** Lawmakers focused on a discrepancy between Lutnick's 2023 podcast claims—where he stated he severed all ties with Epstein in 2005—and evidence showing continued interaction years later.
    * **2012 Island Visit:** Lutnick confirmed a visit to Epstein’s private island in 2012 but defended it as a "family vacation" lunch that lasted only one hour.
    * **Documentary Evidence:** Emails from 2011 published by the Department of Justice show Lutnick met with Epstein multiple times well after the 2005 cutoff he previously claimed.
* **The "Room" Defense:** During the transcribed interview, Lutnick reportedly attempted to redefine his previous statement that he would "never again be in a room" with Epstein.
    * **Semantic Pivot:** According to Rep. Yassamin Ansari, Lutnick argued that his previous comments meant he would never be in a room with Epstein *alone* as a man, despite evidence of group settings and family visits.
    * **Claims of Ignorance:** Lutnick testified that in 2012, he was unaware of Epstein’s 2008 "sweetheart" plea deal or the specific allegations regarding the abuse of minors.

## Partisan Conflict over Committee Findings
* **Democratic Criticism:** Rep. Yassamin Ansari (D-AZ) characterized Lutnick as "evasive, nervous, and dishonest," calling for his immediate resignation.
    * **Body Language:** Ansari noted that while the transcript is revealing, it will not capture the "defensiveness" and "body language" displayed during the 4.5-hour session.
* **Republican Defense:** Chairman James Comer (R-KY) accused Democrats of misrepresenting the closed-door testimony to the media.
    * **Fact-Checking:** Comer urged the public to wait for the official transcript to see that Democrats were "telling stuff that was said that was not said."
    * **White House Stance:** The Biden-Harris administration has so far maintained confidence in Secretary Lutnick despite the intensifying scrutiny.

## Release of Epstein’s Purported Suicide Note
* **Origins of the Note:** A federal judge unsealed a brief, unsigned note found by Epstein's former cellmate, Nicholas Tartaglione, following a failed suicide attempt in the summer of 2019.
    * **Discovery Location:** The note was found hidden inside a novel in the cell Epstein shared with Tartaglione at the Metropolitan Correctional Center (MCC) in Manhattan.
    * **Timing:** This note predates Epstein's eventual death by several weeks and was not included in the original "Epstein Files" release.
* **Content and Significance:** The note includes the line: "It is a treat to be able to choose one's time to say goodbye."
    * **Forensic Status:** The Justice Department has supported the release for transparency but has not yet officially authenticated the handwriting as Epstein’s.
    * **Conspiracy Implications:** Analysts suggest the note may clarify Epstein's state of mind and intent to self-harm, potentially countering long-standing conspiracy theories regarding his death.

## Notable Quotes

> "Howard Lutnick is a pathological liar who is enabling the most egregious cover-up in American history... he doubled down and tried to say that he was not lying in that podcast."
> — **Rep. Yassamin Ansari (D-AZ)**

> "I will never be in the room with that disgusting person ever again. So I was never in the room with him socially, for business, or even for philanthropy. If that guy was there, I wasn't going, because he's gross."
> — **Howard Lutnick (Commerce Secretary)**, *referring to his October 2023 public statement*

> "This is a habit of the Democrats on this committee coming out, telling you all stuff that was said that was not said. I hope that when you get the transcripts, you fact check them."
> — **Rep. James Comer (R-KY)**

> "They investigated me for months, found nothing. It is a treat to be able to choose one’s time to say goodbye. No fun, not worth it."
> — **Jeffrey Epstein** (attributed), *from the unsealed 2019 note*

briefings.title: Extreme Mortman: When DC Laughed at Itself: Dan Glickman and the Golden Age of Political Comedy
briefings.tldr: Former Secretary of Agriculture Dan Glickman argues that self-deprecating humor is an essential, yet vanishing, tool for effective political leadership and bipartisan cooperation.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Former Secretary of Agriculture Dan Glickman argues that self-deprecating humor is an essential, yet vanishing, tool for effective political leadership and bipartisan cooperation.

## The Strategic Value of Political Humor
* **Leadership Utility:** Glickman cites President Eisenhower’s belief that a sense of humor is essential for leadership, as it makes a leader more likable and persuasive.
* **Self-Deprecation:** **Defusing Criticism:** Glickman posits that when politicians highlight their own "blemishes" through humor, it takes the "edge off" the jokes made by others and humanizes them to a skeptical public.
* **The "Carson" Model vs. Modern Comedy:**
    * Glickman contrasts the "low intensity," unifying humor of Johnny Carson with the "high intensity," overtly partisan humor of modern late-night hosts like Stephen Colbert and Jimmy Kimmel. 
    * He argues that modern political comedy often prevents viewers from "relaxing," whereas classic humor helped bridge divides.

## Bipartisanship and the "Golden Age" of Cooperation
* **The Dole-Clinton Dynamic:** Despite being political rivals, President Bill Clinton and Senate Minority Leader Bob Dole maintained a genuine fondness for one another.
* **Unlikely Advocacy:** **Secretary of Agriculture Appointment:** Glickman reveals that Bob Dole (a Republican) was the primary advocate who convinced Bill Clinton (a Democrat) to appoint Glickman to the Cabinet after Glickman lost his 1994 re-election bid.
* **Confirmation Record:** Glickman was confirmed by the Senate with a **93-0 vote**, a feat he believes would be nearly impossible in the current polarized political environment.

## Career Transitions: From the Heartland to Hollywood
* **USDA Leadership:** As Secretary, Glickman navigated the transition of American agriculture into the 21st century, focusing on innovation and maintaining the "envy of the world" status of the U.S. food system.
* **MPAA Tenure:** After the USDA, Glickman served as Chairman and CEO of the Motion Picture Association of America (MPAA). 
    * **Industry Focus:** His work centered on intellectual property, film piracy, and overseeing the movie rating system.
    * **Personal Connection:** His favorite film is *Animal House*, which he claims mirrored his own chaotic fraternity experience at the University of Michigan (1962–1966).

## Advocacy for Transparency and C-SPAN
* **Early Support:** Glickman was a seminal supporter of C-SPAN, working alongside founder Brian Lamb (whom he met while interning in the 1960s).
* **Institutional Access:** Glickman played a key role in the effort to allow C-SPAN cameras into the House of Representatives, arguing that it was vital for the public—and Congress members themselves—to see the legislative process in action.

## Notable Quotes

> "The key to late-night political humor is that it targets those qualities that we, the politicians, don't want you to see. But if we were to bring out our blemishes into the open, it takes the edge off the jokes that other people make about us." — **Dan Glickman**

> "Dole said to me, 'I just have one question for you... Will this get you out of Kansas forever?' I said, 'Well, if you're asking if I would ever run against you, no.' And so Dole was a big helper." — **Dan Glickman**

> "I decided that I had an interesting career... but I also felt like the humor that exists in this country is kind of missing in action when it comes to natural self-deprecating humor in the political sphere." — **Dan Glickman**

briefings.title: FULL REMARKS: Brazil's Lula Talks U.S. Relations, Trump Meeting, Trade, Tariff & Global Order | AC1N
briefings.tldr: President Lula characterized his three-hour meeting with Donald Trump as a breakthrough in consolidating Brazil-US relations, highlighted by a new 30-day mandate to resolve trade disputes and a proposed joint task force to combat the financial structures of organized crime.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
President Lula characterized his three-hour meeting with Donald Trump as a breakthrough in consolidating Brazil-US relations, highlighted by a new 30-day mandate to resolve trade disputes and a proposed joint task force to combat the financial structures of organized crime.

## Trade and Economic Re-engagement
* **Commercial Rebalancing:** Lula addressed Brazil’s current $14 billion trade deficit with the U.S., urging a return to the 20th-century status where the U.S. was Brazil’s primary partner.
    * **30-Day Working Group:** Following disagreements over tariff levels (Brazil cites a 2.7% average while the U.S. claims higher rates on specific goods), the leaders agreed to have their respective trade ministers present a resolution proposal within 30 days.
* **Countering Chinese Hegemony:** Lula noted that the U.S. lost commercial dominance in Brazil around 2008. He specifically invited U.S. firms to compete in infrastructure auctions (railroads and highways) where Chinese companies currently dominate.
* **Technology and Energy:**
    * **Data Centers:** Brazil is open to hosting international data centers provided they produce their own energy; Lula stated Brazil will not subsidize energy for data that is sent abroad.

## Strategic Minerals and Sovereignty
* **Critical Minerals Legislation:** Lula highlighted the recent passage of a law treating critical minerals as a matter of national sovereignty, establishing a council under the Presidency to coordinate these resources.
* **Value-Added Processing:** While inviting investment from the U.S., China, Germany, and Japan, Lula emphasized that Brazil will no longer be a "mere exporter" of raw materials.
    * **Strategic Goal:** Partners must invest in internal transformation and processing within Brazil to share in the wealth of "rare earths."
* **Resource Mapping:** Brazil currently only has detailed knowledge of 30% of its mineral territory; the administration aims to reach 100% through these new partnerships.

## Security and Organized Crime
* **A Financial Approach:** Lula proposed moving away from traditional military-base models to focus on destroying the financial potential of criminal factions, which he described as "multinational corporations" embedded in politics and business.
* **Shared Responsibility:**
    * **Arms and Money Laundering:** Lula reminded Trump that many weapons reaching Brazil originate in the U.S. and that significant money laundering occurs within American states.
    * **Economic Alternatives:** Argued that drug production in Latin America can only be stopped if farmers are offered viable economic alternatives and guaranteed buyers for legal crops.
* **Regional Cooperation:** Brazil invited the U.S. to participate in the intelligence base in Manaus, which coordinates with all South American countries to monitor borders.

## Global Diplomacy and UN Reform
* **UN Security Council Reform:** Lula urged the "P5" (U.S., China, Russia, France, UK) to take responsibility for expanding the Council to include Brazil, India, Germany, Japan, and African nations. 
    * He argued that the 1945 geopolitical structure is obsolete and that the current veto power prevents the UN from stopping "slaughter" in places like Palestine.
* **Conflict Mediation:** 
    * **Iran and Cuba:** Lula offered Brazil’s services as a mediator, referencing his 2010 nuclear negotiations with Iran. He noted that the U.S. signaled it does not intend to invade Cuba.
    * **Venezuela:** Expressed hope for a democratic resolution under the current mandate while emphasizing his preference for dialogue over "bellicose" narratives.
* **Diplomatic Visas:** Lula personally delivered a list to Trump of Brazilian officials and citizens (including a 10-year-old child) whose U.S. visas remain revoked, requesting a review of these sanctions.

## Personal Relationship and Sovereignty
* **Relationship Dynamics:** Lula described the rapport as "love at first sight" and "chemistry," noting that a "smiling Trump is better than a frowning one."
* **Electoral Non-Interference:** Lula dismissed concerns about Trump’s influence on future Brazilian elections, stating that just as he respects U.S. sovereignty, he expects the U.S. to let the Brazilian people decide their own destiny.

> "I believe much more in dialogue than in war... I don't have a bellicose vocation. My vocation is for dialogue, believing in the power of the narrative and the power of persuasion." — **President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva**

> "The public machine is eternal. The President has an expiration date... we have a four-year mandate, things have to happen. We must establish goal plans for people to fulfill." — **President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva**

> "We don't want to repeat what happened with silver in Latin America, or with gold... where the ore was sent out. With rare earths, we are going to change behavior. We want Brazil to be the great winner of this wealth nature gave us." — **President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva**
